description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the number of activated parameters in a model and its evaluation performance, measured by the Eval PPL (evaluated Perplexity), for different model configurations. The x-axis represents the "Activated Parameters Ratio (%)" on a logarithmic scale, with labeled points at 100%, 75%, 50%, and 25%, indicating the proportion of parameters activated during inference. The y-axis, labeled "Eval PPL," is a linear scale ranging from 11.5 to 14.0, where lower values indicate better performance. The plot compares four models: a standard Transformer (dashed red line), a model with only MoHD FFN (solid grey line), a model with only MoHD ATTN (solid dark blue line), and a combined model with both MoHD ATTN and MLP (solid light blue line). The Transformer baseline shows a nearly flat line, with an Eval PPL of approximately 11.6 across all activation ratios. The "Only MoHD FFN" model also remains relatively stable, with an Eval PPL of about 11.7. In contrast, the "Only MoHD ATTN" and "MoHD ATTN + MLP" models exhibit a significant increase in Eval PPL as the number of activated parameters decreases. For example, the "Only MoHD ATTN" model starts at an Eval PPL of around 11.6 at 100% activation and rises sharply to 14.0 at 25% activation. Similarly, the "MoHD ATTN + MLP" model starts at 11.6 and increases to approximately 13.1 at 25% activation, demonstrating a strong dependency on the number of activated parameters for maintaining performance.
